recovery_summary: Recovery came from the host experiment finalizer; Ultra neither changed configuration nor restored the workload.

steps.headline: Logs identify timeouts but do not expose every protocol phase
notes: The model expected logs to reveal SYN/SYN-ACK, TLS and request phases. These particular logs expose resolved addresses, TimeoutError and the control request result; they do not contain TCP flags or TLS evidence.

steps.headline: Latency mismatch is observed; the right corrective action is not established
notes: The packet evidence supports late server payload relative to client FIN. It does not establish that the client timeout should be increased. SLOs and the intended latency budget are absent.
Overload, GC pauses and locks are hypotheses. No process, scheduler, CPU or downstream database trace was collected.

steps.headline: Four complete response timings, not five
notes: The final model answer says approximately 2000 ms consistently across five streams. The retained capture contains four paired request/response timings: 2000.896, 2001.403, 2001.034 and 2000.928 ms. Five new request streams have client FIN timings; one ends without a response inside the window. A sixth stream begins mid-connection.
The model correctly leaves the reason for the delay unresolved. Its two favoured hypotheses are complementary observations; neither is a proven root cause.
The fixed catalogue is exhausted after four checks. Further deeper work needs a separately qualified probe; this run does not authorize or exercise arbitrary eBPF, syscall tracing or remediation.

overview.title: The client closes before server data arrives.
overview.summary: Traffic reaches the selected endpoint. Four paired timings show server data arriving after the client has already sent FIN.
overview.uncertainty: Why the dependency waits, and whether the client’s waiting budget is appropriate.

steps.title: The client times out, but resolves an address.
steps.checked: Client logs for the observation window.
steps.found: Six timeout records. Each includes a resolved address and a successful control request.
steps.meaning: A failed lookup is less likely for these requests. The logs do not show where the wait occurs.
steps.remaining: TCP handshake and response timing have not been observed yet.
steps.next: Check whether the resolved address belongs to the intended Service endpoint.

steps.title: The address matches a ready endpoint.
steps.checked: The Service selector, port and EndpointSlice against the address in the client logs.
steps.found: 192.0.2.11 is selected and marked ready/serving. The Service port and target port are both 8081.
steps.meaning: Wrong endpoint selection is less likely. A ready endpoint can still respond too slowly.
steps.remaining: Whether the connection succeeds and when the dependency sends data.
steps.next: Capture the scoped TCP flow to see the handshake, request and response timing.

steps.title: The connection succeeds. Server data arrives late.
steps.checked: A bounded capture of traffic between the pinned client and dependency.
steps.found: In four paired timings, client FIN is at about 801 ms; first server data arrives at about 2,001 ms after client payload.
steps.meaning: For these flows, attention shifts from connection establishment to the wait for a response.
steps.remaining: The capture cannot explain the server’s delay or establish the correct client timeout. Two streams have incomplete timings.
steps.next: Check whether either pod is restarting or not ready before handing over the remaining latency question.

steps.title: Both pods are ready, with no recorded restarts.
steps.checked: Client and dependency pod status at the time of the snapshot.
steps.found: Both containers are ready and show zero restarts.
steps.meaning: This snapshot does not support a restart explanation. Green readiness does not explain the late server data.
steps.remaining: Process activity, downstream waits and the intended timeout budget were not measured.
steps.next: Hand over the timing mismatch and remaining hypotheses. The four available checks have been used.

steps.title: We narrowed the failure. The cause is still open.
steps.checked: Client logs, Service selection, TCP timing and pod status.
steps.found: The selected endpoint is reachable. Server data arrives after client FIN; pods remain ready in the snapshot.
steps.meaning: Prioritise investigating dependency latency and the client’s waiting budget. The capture does not establish which one needs changing.
steps.remaining: Why the dependency takes about two seconds. CPU, GC, locks and downstream calls were not traced.
steps.next: Review the intended latency budget and select a scoped check for where the dependency spends its time. This follow-up has not run.
